overview: A gene is one unit of heredity; the genome is the complete set of all genetic material in an organism.
genZNote: Gene is one song. Genome is the entire discography.

aspects.label: Scope
aspects.valueA: A single functional unit of DNA coding for one product (usually a protein or RNA).
aspects.valueB: The entire DNA content of an organism, including all genes and non-coding sequences.

aspects.label: Size
aspects.valueA: A few hundred to a few million base pairs.
aspects.valueB: The human genome is about 3.2 billion base pairs.

aspects.label: Count in Humans
aspects.valueB: One genome per organism, containing all of its genes plus regulatory and non-coding DNA.

overlay.examHighYieldNote: The Human Genome Project sequenced the entire genome, not just individual genes.
overlay.memoryTrick: Genome = genes + everything else, all together.
overlay.commonMisconception: The genome is not made up only of genes — most of the human genome is non-coding DNA.
